item.title: The Though Farmer
item.description: An SCP that uses the 'thought energy' of people to gain more, and further its own objectives.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is a humanoid SCP whose main objective appears to be the collection of, what will be labeled for ease of understanding, thought energy. The exact nature of this energy is unknown, however it is known that SCP-XXXX is able to use this energy to influence or cause events. It is also understood that each human has roughly equal amounts of thought energy and that animals posses thought energy in lesser quantities, with more intelligent and larger animals possessing more than other species. SCP-XXXX typically gains this energy by gathering followers for cults or religions it leads or influences, however other methods have been recorded, with varying success.

+ show block
– hide block

The nature of the cults ran by SCP-XXXX is almost always non-violent, as SCP-XXXX seems to be be benevolent towards human and animal life and most recorded incidents of violence from an SCP-XXXX ran cult are directed towards insects and micro-organisms. SCP-XXXX begins its extraction process by introducing a religion or cult it is involved with to it's target, via use of its existing thought energy. SCP-XXXX will then manipulate it's target to focus on its cult by appealing to things the target enjoys, such as hobbies. It is at this stage that the target will either decide to become involved in the cult and proceed to the next stage, or will decide that they are uninterested, at which point SCP-XXXX will no longer interfere with their lives. If the target does decide to become involved, they will begin to become involved in the cult. Common activities at this stage include regular prayer times and regular meeting, both usually on a weekly basis. After taking part in these activities for about one to two and a half months, the target will enter the final stage. During this stage, the target will become more and more involved in cult activities until they take up a significant amount of the target's available time. The target will begin to sacrifice all 'optional' activities, including spending time with a significant other to make time for cult activities, however it will still take part in necessary daily activities, including eating meals, going to work and basic hygiene activities such as taking a bath or shower and brushing their teeth. During this stage the target will also have decreased cognitive functions, recording on average a 25% decrease in cognitive functions. There is currently no known way to exit this stage, barring termination of the subject, however research is ongoing. There are currently 2260 people under the effects of the

SCP-XXXX itself is a non-corporeal entity that is capable of appearing as almost any animal or person, including animals and people that do not currently exist. SCP-XXXX only appears to communicate with individuals it does not intend to use to gain additional thought energy. SCP-XXXX is capable of appearing in dreams of individuals it is trying to effect, as well as appearing in the 'real' world (For lack of a better word.). SCP-XXXX appears unable to manifest on electronic display devices though it can still appear to the viewer(s) of the device, but does not show up on any recordings of the encounter. There has also been no recorded physical interaction with SCP-XXXX to date, and it is incapable of moving objects, however while within and individuals dream it is capable of moving objects. SCP-XXXX has also been observed on several occasions interacting with foundation personnel. It appears to have no desire to harm foundation however due to the effects of SCP-XXXX it is advised that unnecessary communication with SCP-XXXX be kept to a minimum.
SCP-XXXX current motives are unknown, however there are some recorded conversations between foundation staff and SCP-XXXX that are on display in it's file.

Central Narrative: This SCP article focuses on SCP-XXXX's activities, what religions and cults SCP-XXXX has interfered with in history (that the foundation can find) SCP-XXXX's current endeavours, it's motives and communication with the foundation and, ultimately what it will do with its power (besides get more).

Hook: Theres a lot I could put here, but I envision the main hook as the process that SCP-XXXX 'gains' additional people, as well as its interactions with the foundation and its end goal with what it wants to accomplish (which will partly be a mystery, to maintain intrigue.).

Notes: While the whole emphasis on SCP-XXXX's motives and goals seems lacking in this greenlight/ idea critique post, I will include some conversations that foundation personnel have had with the SCP that will go more in depth on the subject. It is very hard to include that here.
And yes, I do know that this is a very long post for the idea critique forum, but I believe that I at least have to describe this SCP in some detail, as what I have included here is already quite sparse. Sorry if its a long read though. (IDK how to do the minimizing/clickable box thing very well.)

The house is found to have its own microclimate similar to the Pacific Northwest, and its ecosystem is self-perpetuating due to the anomalous rabbits. Central Narrative: It’s revealed through the found documents, an owner’s journals, that they had two rabbits. Before they could get them spade and neutered, the vets office closed due to quarantine. Unable to be contained, going so far as to teleport, the male rabbits kept escaping and creating more litters. The owners hired the city compost to take their quickly escalating piles of rabbit poo.

Over time, firs, ferns, blackberries, and other Pacific Northwest foliage grows out of the rabbit poo at an expedited rate. The owners, and housemates, slowly turn into rabbit-people when parasitic baby rabbits burrow into the base of their skulls. (Similar to the Goa’uld from Stargate).

Two Foundation agents are sent to investigate the house and they traverse room to room to figure out the ill fate of the owners. They are chased out of the house by angry rabbits, and rabbit-people.

item.title: Kamen Rider but it's SCP
item.description: I once threatened someone I'd write this, but is it any good?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action

Elevator Pitch: If you're going to get a Magic Man to help make your superhero dreams come true, be sure you know what the hell you're doing. Otherwise you'll turn your friends into bugs and make demons out of your little sister's cancer.

+ Central Narrative
- Hide

A dumb teenager who's equal parts edgy and idealistic decides the world would be better if his favorite Japanese superhero were in it for realz. So he goes to his local Magic Man to ask for some magic, which he gets. He of course has no idea how to use it properly, so testing quickly starts going wrong. Using the magic superhero belt too long/too many times turns the wearer into a pile of bugs. Distraught after losing at least one friend, he reevaluates why he's doing this. The point of being a hero isn't doing cool moves or beating up bad guys, you see. It's about making a real change in the world. Cue a little bit more magic to try and help his little sister's cancer. Cancer turns into monsters/demons that can be fought in the real world, since you can't Rider Kick cancer without killing a little kid. Our protagonist vanishes after this, as does his sister.

This is later discovered by the Foundation after our would-be hero goes missing and cancer demons start terrorizing SoCal. The demons are the primary object, the belt is the secondary. Said demons can only be contained by someone using the belt (yes, this is a Thing What Makes You Fight Good skip, strike 1, I know), so you've got an MTF that's switching off different members being the 'hero' and fighting cancer demons while hoping desperately the next time they put it on, they don't turn into a pile of bugs. And that's about where the idea ends.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Man, if you're not already here to read SCP articles, I don't know how to hook you.

Additional Notes: Article will include hand-written journal entries with sketches, doodles and likely personally revealing notes.

item.title: Semi-Veil breaking Parawatch SCP idea
item.description: Parawatch getting their hands on a easily demonstrable anomaly and the Foundation scrambling to cover it up.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Action/Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP format with an extended incident log

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation works hard to cover up anomalies, having extensive measures to prevent word of the Paranormal getting out. But the internet is a popular thing, especially among conspiracy theorists.

Central Narrative: A simple anomaly is discovered by WWS. It's a frog that when a picture is taken of it, always produces the same photo. Further more, whenever an addition copy of the photo is created, physical or digital, a non-anomalous frog of the same type is formed in the vicinity. The main story of the article comes when a member of the Parawatch community gets their hands on one of the photos and discovers it's properties. They send it to the rest of Parawatch who continue to send it and copy it like crazy. The Foundation learns about it but their normal strategies such as taking the picture down and visual amnestics don't work due to the paranoia of Parawatch and them saving copies to hard-drives. This comes to a head when the Foundation resorts to a complete take-down of the Parawatch wiki and the physical administration of amnestics to all exposed members, draining significant resources and giving the Parawatch community a lot to speculate on. The article closes out with a note regarding the difficulty of maintaining the veil in the internet age and about being thankful the image wasn't memetic.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A simple anomaly and a non-anomalous group almost breaking the veil.

Additional Notes: I am considering adding an interview with a Parawatch member, but am unsure if the Foundation would do that sort of thing.

item.title: Boulevard of Broken Dreams
item.description: A way to be free of past burdens.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Emotional

Page Layout: The "standard" SCP article format, with a description and then test logs hidden in a collapsible. The test logs will be formatted:

 Subject: Items: [Location]:Item ... Afterwards:

Elevator Pitch: A road on which objects relating to your past dreams, goals, and desires appear (out of reach). As you walk along it, past burdens are "freed" from you.

Central Narrative: Disconnected stories of the people that walk on the road, told by the objects that they encounter. For instance:

  • An burnt out ethics committee member who wanted to "bring justice" when he was younger (a discolored robe, a trap with a hole in it, a corroded pen,…, a colorless foundation site), after stepping off of the road he resigns from the foundation.
  • A terrorist who was a revolutionary. (A torn police cap, burnt money, a rusted guillotine,…, his own corpse), who puts up less resistance after.
  • A doctor who wanted to save lives. (A firefighter coat, a broken down gravestone,…, a hospital in the distance). Returned to foundation work with increased score on the Foundation Personnel Wellness Exam.
  • …
+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP aims to tell the story of people's lives through the test logs, which are just lists of items, without the "human" in them. There are no notes on theorized meanings, and the reader is free to draw their own conclusion from the objects and their location on the road.

Additional Notes: I don't quite know how "strong(?)" to make the effect of giving up your past dreams yet. item.content:encoded:
Hey howdy hey, so I'm writing a tale at the moment that predominantly revolves around a crime scene. Thing is, I don't actually know very much about how actual crime scene procedures work, as the most popular point of reference tends to be dramatized TV shows.

I realise that in order to keep stuff interesting I'll need to strike a decent balance between real-world procedure and something a little more fictitious, but I'm not entirely sure where to look for real-world references. I've done some research, but I end up with a mixed bag of results that refer to how various countries handle it.

I'm looking for details of crime scene procedure as it would be in the real world particularly for the US - what kinda staff will be present, who's allowed where, how much can be done on-site that would contribute to the investigation, etc.
The crime takes place indoors (an apartment), and involves a dead body, if those details matter at all.

Articles for reference would be good, and if there's any online short story type deals that exist out there (I've had no luck finding any that aren't books) that would be fantastic.

item.title: Buzzcut
item.description: A buzzer from the 1950's that grants you irresistible charisma.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Fantasy

Elevator Pitch: It's a barber buzzer. Upon using it on one's head, the individual starts receiving more attention than usual. Overtime, as hair grows, the attention diminishes, unless one cuts again, and instead attention increases. Attention, as well as sex appeal. Continuing the process allows the user to have increasing and overwhelming charisma to the extent that they can influence first people, then towns, then world events.

Central Narrative: The buzzer was found to be in the possession of an artifact dealer, and was purchased by the owner of a 50's themed diner to be placed in a safe with other memorabilia. Upon discovery by the Foundation, the dive owner says the girl he bought it from claims it was used by Elvis to cut his hair. After testing the piece is found to be non anamolous, placed in confinement, however an agent over the testing steals it to resell it, but not before trying it on his own head. He begins to notice his life change.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact the the influence builds on itself to make the user more and more powerful, and can be transferred if one single hair is buzzed on another man or woman. The buzzer also increases the physical strength of the individual and performance of physiological functions, to the extent that the user can not only become stronger than possible for a human, but also have a faster metabolism (speed), more god like features, and be a far greater sexy badboy/girl than humanly possible.

Additional Notes: After non-use of about a week, all influence dies out. It isn't saved within the buzzer. This is why, if the Elvis fact is true, Elvis, nor any of the other users' influence, is transferred to new users. Any stretch beyond humanly possible abilities granted by the buzzer is unnoticed by individuals, due to the overwhelming charisma, and is brushed off. There is no proper way to cut your hair with the buzzer, but upon doing so, everyone will love your haircut.

Elevator Pitch: The object swaps two aspects (body parts/memories/reality of their life) of a person with a new one, seemingly from its "collection" of obtained aspects. Since an unknown number of exchanges have occurred, over an unknown time/places, it has an unknowable number of aspects in its collection.

Central Narrative: Minimal. The testing logs will add mystery around the objects age/origins and purpose, suggesting alien/extra-dimensional life. Since the object can alter reality, detailed records and logs need to be kept in order to keep track of reality alterations.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The object removes aspects of a person and gives a brand new one. The removal of aspects could kill or dramatically change a person, even removing people/companies/ideas related to them. The new aspects can be memories, new organs, or reality altering itself as well. The testing logs will start with mundane things, eg gaining memories of another person, growing a new limb etc, and will progress to stranger exchanges where friends/family cease to exist, or they gain non-human knowledge. Adding to the intrigue is that every aspect "given" is assumed to have been taken at some stage, suggesting that the object has altered reality many times in the past in unknown ways.

Elevator Pitch: Basically, this scp is an anomalous man from a different dimension in which the laws of physics are fundamentally different. It's because of this difference that he has the ability to manipulate gravity. His upbringing and childlike curiosity provided the perfect origin story for a modern superhero with a scientific alter ego. By day he was a lab coat pushing the limits of his abilities to fully understand gravity and it's effects, by night a merciless vigilante obliterating local crime with an iron fist.

+ show block
– hide block

Now, I know what it looks like but stay with me, this isn't just another superhero. In fact, the true danger of this scp came from his day job as a scientist. His continuous experiments yielded amazing discoveries about what he could do, but it eventually led to the collapse of the universe as we know it. The collapse of the universe damned him to just exist in an existence in which he was the only thing that excited. Madness had claimed him after a millennia of solitude, but he didn't spend his time in the void laying down. He used this time to further study his ability. Eventually he was able to feel the connection between time and gravity. This led his ability to manipulate time. From there he formulated a plan to send himself back in time to kill his younger self before he collapses the universe. However, do to his mental instability he was slain his younger self. That younger version of himself grew to repeat history/the future and collapsed the universe, went mad, discovered time travel, and repeated the plan to kill his younger self. This time however, he remembered how he defeated his older self and didn't fall for the same tactic he used when he was younger. This caused the fight to last a while longer than the first fight. However, the younger version of himself still came out on top do to his mental edge. This younger version of himself repeated the same cycle extending the fight just a bit longer. As the cycle continued the scale of the battle grew larger, so did the foundation's involvement. This only served to escalate the situation as it eventually led to a broken masquerade. This cycle repeated until the battle was the cause of the collapsed universe. The cycle finally ended when he decided to instead travel farther back in time and seek out the foundation to contain his younger self before he grows up to become a threat. The conversation with a mad man didn't get nearly as far as the scp article he brought back with him as proof of his claims. The article inside the article is the one he brought back with him and the over all article will be the whole story.

Central Narrative: It's a tragic story of a hero being his only threat. Eventually ending the narrative before it starts.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The very deeply rooted story.

item.title: SCP-TBD: The Extradimensional Grand Station
item.description: What if there was a subway system that went everywhere
item.content:encoded:
What if there was a subway system that went everywhere and everywhen? What if it went to pasts, presents, and futures where events unfolded differently? What wonderous possibilities could be waiting? And what untold horrors?

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up a lot of space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Document/Exploratory File

Elevator Pitch:

  • Entrance to anomaly first found in the form of an undocumented stairway in the New York City Subway shortly after 9/11.
  • This stairway, officially listed as SCP-TBD, also known as the Extradimensional Stairway by SCP personnel, leads to a massive series of passageways, officially listed as SCP-TBD-1
  • Visitors are guided by instances of artificial lifeforms consisting of programable matter/nanites. These instances take the form of the species they are interacting with.
  • This facility is controlled by a highly advanced AI system.
+ show block
– hide block
  • Due to the size of this facility, transportation to entrances are provided by a series of vacuum trains. According to readings provided by the onboard interfaces and the body-suit sensors worn by exploratory teams, these trains are capable of accelerating quickly to hypersonic speeds, but without producing the associated g-forces that would normally kill their occupants.

Central Narrative: Anomaly is a massive underground system that leads to an as yet undetermined number of places, including different planets and alternate realities. Various different species and alternate versions of humanity use this system, and the facility can be inhabited by a minimum of beings ranging in the thousands on any day.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The finished article will list exploratory expeditions to different planets in the prime reality, as well as into different timelines. Many different references to different SCPs and settings will be included, such as instances of SCP-682 being escorted back to their stairway entrance, one by an android dragging him in a stun net (kicking, screaming, and shouting insults and threats), while the witnessing MTF just looks on, and an instance of a reality where the Foundation and anomalies has been disclosed to the public.

Additional Notes:
This is my first SCP entry. I currently have two versions of this working in my head: one is more positive and optimistic, and is my preferred direction. Then there is another that is abandoned, inhabited by an insane AI, malfunctioning killer androids, and horrors from alternate dimensions that have wandered into the system. Idea is extrapolated from some dreams I've had in the past, namely the vast vacuum train system and stairways that go deep underground and into a maze of passageways.

item.title: You're It (SCP concept)
item.description: An affliction that causes individuals to attack others and pass on the affliction
item.content:encoded:
An affliction that causes individuals to attack others and pass on the affliction to survivors of the attacks. Those affected by this SCP will cease to be afflicted after passing it on.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

This SCP is a phenomenon that causes afflicted individuals to quickly become more hostile and violent towards others, as well as giving them increased physical strength and resistance to injury. The exact cause of this is unknown, as no pathogen or other potential source has yet to be identified. This SCP will likely cause affected individuals to attack nearby people, often resulting in their deaths. Those who survive these attacks will begin to exhibit the same anomalous effects as their attacker, while the attacker will slowly lose the aggression and increased strength.

Those that have "passed on" the SCP have a moderate chance to die of multiple organ failure after the effects have subsided, and those that live retain memories of their actions while under the influence of this SCP. Should the current carrier of this SCP die before passing it on, it will instead be passed on to the carrier's killer. If the carrier was not killed by a sapient being, the SCP will instead pass on to a random individual, where nearer individuals are more likely to be afflicted.

This SCP is contained via an afflicted D-Class personnel inside a reinforced concrete humanoid containment chamber. The D-Class is kept alive as long as possible, and their vitals are constantly monitored. Additional D-Class personnel are introduced into the chamber to allow the SCP to be passed on. The previous carrier will be tranquilized via remotely controlled sentries before they can kill the new carrier. The previous carrier, now sedated, is removed from the chamber and amnestics are administered.

item.title: Heartbeat of Iceland
item.description: A series of heartbeat-like sounds coming from deep lakes around Iceland.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery/Horror

Page Layout: ACS header, basic layout, tons of audio recordings and exploration logs

Elevator Pitch: Series of sounds that resemble heartbeats, only found in deep lakes in Iceland, each with varying frequencies and loudness. The sounds are quite rare and cause mishaps in reality in a wide area around it.

Central Narrative: The heartbeats last for 20-75 seconds, and range in frequency, loudness, and location. Heartbeats are relatively rare (1-3 times a year) but can be very troubling for the area around it.

Heartbeats come in pairs of 2 "pumps", in this case, sound. Once a heartbeat starts, the pumps cause vibrations in the land, seemingly wavy land. Everything the sound can be heard is effected.
Here's a list of each possible reality-bending scenario

  • Vibrations in the land (wavy-like land)
  • Mountains deforming in a very unnatural way
  • Water vortexes
  • "cracks" in the air, where a black spot fills the crack
  • Clouds taking shape of humanoid figures
  • Talbon's Ring (a high-frequency ring that burst eardrums and rarely kills an organism)
  • The sky turning into dark, even during bright days
  • Temperature suddenly shooting up or increasing drastically
  • Altered heartbeats of humans (matches the lake's heartbeat)

These are the only known effects of the heartbeat, but in later logs, more will appear (creepier and deadlier). A heartbeat can have serious effects on the ecosystem, and cause mass death amongst organisms, and heavily deformed land.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A decent reality-bender that has some good potential, even though it probably has a LOT to work on.

Additional Notes: Suggestions for editing needed :)

item.title: Counting Sheep
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Sci-fi

Page Layout: An SCP Article that has collapsible sections with up to date versions of the SCP’s description, containment procedures and so on. (This is necessary due to the nature of this SCP.)

Elevator Pitch: A herd of nine migrating sheep (SCP-XXXX-1) that causes sudden and inexplicable somnolence for subjects inside a 1km spherical radius. The herd exhibits no biological anomalies with the exception that none seem to need sustenance nor excrete waste, and at the time of discovery seemed to be in a pattern of continuous migration. The nine sheep are living embodiments of nine identical music boxes that contain the mental essence of a child that suffered from fatal familial insomnia.

Central Narrative: The SCP was brought to the foundation's attention after a 2km chain car crash happened on a highway caused by the sudden onset of fatigue of multiple drivers. The foundation successfully captured the herd by estimating and setting up traps along its migratory route. SCP-XXXX is contained within a circular metal fence to prevent unauthorized personnel from entering SCP-XXXX-1’s effective radius.

+ show block
– hide block

SCP-XXXX-1 transformed into SCP-XXXX-2, a set of nine identical music boxes a month into containment. However, when music was played from all nine boxes simultaneously, they transformed back. The discovery of SCP-XXXX-2’s abilities led to the Slumbering Prison Incident at the foundation where the SCP placed all living organisms on the site which SCP-XXXX was contained under a state of somnolence. During the incident, all nine sheep broke out of the facility and began retracing their steps back to their place of origin. Before a team could be mobilized, all the sheep stopped in front of a small house on the edge of a city. When a team of SCP agents got there, all the sheep turned back into music boxes. Inside of all the boxes, there was a new engraving that says “Mom, I am home.”

The last owner of the house was a single mother with a son whose dreams of being an adventurer is shattered by fatal familial insomnia. The son started to develop symptoms at the age of 6 and was bedridden until he died at the age of 15. The mother went missing a month after the death of her son. Video recordings were found of the mother giving the son one music box that looks identical to one instance of SCP-XXXX-2 during his birthday. Every year he suffered from insomnia, he was given the same music box.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This story is about a child chasing his dream and his relationship with his mother makes it interesting.

If I write one more verse of rhyme

But honestly it's been a slice,

Keep hanging on;

Here's to next year.
